pooling_claim: PRE-REGISTERED, and it is the reason this wave matters beyond its own four seeds. The 57-id family needs 8 seeds; W41 gave 4 and this wave gives 4. Pooling W41+W42 has so far been decided by TREE OBJECT HASH, and by that criterion these two waves are different trees and may not be pooled. The hash criterion is wrong here, and the demonstration is a compiler, not prose: the only file that changed (bots/BotLib/hero_chaos_knight.lua, commit 9053d199) compiles under lua5.1 to a bytecode listing that, once pointer addresses and line numbers are normalised away, differs in ZERO lines from W41's. Note two weaker checks that would NOT have settled it: `luac -s` md5 differed (so a naive bytecode-hash oracle says 'different tree'), and the repo's own strip_lua_comments heuristic left an 18-byte residue (trailing whitespace) before line-wise comparison agreed. => Batch desk's reading: W41 and W42 measure the SAME tree under the SAME arm and ARE poolable, which would take the 57-id family to 8 seeds in one step. The pooling decision is the director's, not this desk's; this key exists so the claim is on the record BEFORE the numbers land, and cannot be reverse-fitted to them.
